clues: This small mining city lies in the far northeast of Canada. It sits close to the line that splits Quebec from Labrador.
Winter here drags on for about seven long months. One huge block was built to block the harsh wind for homes behind it.
This city was built in the early 1970s by a mining firm. It rose fast to dig rich iron ore from Mont Wright.
One giant block holds homes, shops, a school, a pool, and a hotel. Most folks can live, learn, and play all in one place.
That giant block has a short, bold name: The Wall. It shades the whole town from the wind.
